title: Heart-rate variance asymmetry gives a small external CHF score gain that is uncertain after training and signal-quality checks
abstract: In a locked new-feature test on previously used public cohorts, adding absolute deceleration variance asymmetry to mean NN, SDNN, RMSSD and pNN50 raised external CHF-versus-control AUC from 0.7976 to 0.8321 and lowered log loss from 0.5174 to 0.4818 (33 discovery, 83 external recordings). Fixed-model paired bootstrap intervals were -0.0096 to 0.0881 for delta AUC and -0.0710 to -0.0018 for delta log loss. Including discovery-fit uncertainty widened the log-loss interval to -0.0930 to 0.0304. Adjustment for valid-NN fraction attenuated the log-loss gain to 0.0070 with an interval spanning zero. The predicted lower asymmetry in CHF did not transfer. These results do not establish a reliable clinical biomarker. Separate databases were tested, but enrollment overlap cannot be ruled out. Author checks and byte-identical numerical reruns are supplied.
